issues.description: Method SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice: the problem statement requires calculateTotalPrice to be declared static (shared, operating on the shared static stock), but the solution implements it as an instance method (public int calculateTotalPrice(Meal)). This mismatch between the specification (static) and the provided implementation (instance) can confuse students about the intended design, cause tests or examples that call SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(...) statically to fail, and leads to uncertainty about whether the method should use the shared static stock field directly.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the method signature in SealSaloon to be static to match the specification (e.g., public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal)). Ensure the implementation continues to reference the shared static stock field and update any call sites (tests or example code) to call SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(meal) if they currently call it on an instance. Alternatively, if the intended design is to keep it an instance method, update the problem statement to remove the requirement that calculateTotalPrice be static so the specification and implementation match.
